newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares fall back on U.S. GDP data.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares fall back on U.S. GDP data.

text.p: Austria's ATX index ended with marginal losses on Wednesday, with a surprisingly big jump in first quarter U.S. gross domestic product triggering a late flurry of selling, traders said.
A reluctance to take up fresh positions ahead of the Labour Day holiday tomorrow also capped the market, traders said.
The ATX closed 3.94 points, or 0.33 percent, lower at 1,194.23 -- just off session lows -- after earlier climbing up to 1,212.23.
"We could see some huge price swings on small volume on Friday," said one. "We've got to see what the Americans do, but I think we're going to trade weaker again."
Support for the ATX lies first at 1,190 points, then 1,180.
Of its 21 constituents, 11 shares gained, nine fell and one was unchanged by the close.
The top gainer was microchip maker AMS, up 2.22 percent at 920 ATS, while regional utility EVN led decliners, shedding 2.46 percent to 1,507 ATS.
The all-share Vienna bourse index lost 1.21 points, or 0.27 percent, to 451.55.
The May ATX future fell six points to 1,188 on turnover of 710 contracts.
The Vienna market will be closed for Labour Day on Thursday.
